 :JUDGMENT:
This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.35,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by him in a Road Traffic Accident.
SCCH 15 3 MVC No.2168/2021 2.

The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 17.01.2021 at about 11.00 a.m., when the Petitioner was proceeding in his TVS XL 100 bearing Reg.No.KA52Q9654 from Honnamachanahalli towards Huliyurdurga side and when he reached near K.H. Halli Circle, Amruthuru Durga Road, K. Honnamachanahalli, at that time, the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA520339 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Motorcycle of the Petitioner from behind and caused accident.
Due to this impact, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries to all over the body.
Immediately, after the accident, the Petitioner was taken to Kunigal Government Hospital, wherein he took first aid treatment and then shifted to KIMS hospital and admitted as an inpatient.
Thereafter he was shifted to Jain Hospital, Bengaluru and undergone surgery.
The Petitioner has spent SCCH 15 4 MVC No.2168/2021 Rs.10,00,000/ towards medical expenses and other incidental expenses.
3. Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as a Driver and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/ per month.
The Respondent No.1 is the Owner and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA520339.
Therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
4. In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondents, the Respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.
The Respondent No.2 had appeared before the Court through its Counsel and filed its Objection statement to the main Petition.

5. The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver SCCH 15 5 MVC Gangadharaiah H.S vs Anand on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138655043/
2 No.2168/2021 of the offending vehicle and also the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the expenses incurred for the treatment.
Further it contended that the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA520339 was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
The Respondent No.1 being the owner of the lorry permitted the vehicle to drive in a public place without having valid RC, Permit and FC.
Therefore, it is not liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
On these grounds, the Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the Petition against it.
6. On the rival Pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:

ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 17.01.2021 at about 11.00 a.m, near K.H. Halli circle, Amruthuru Durga Road, K. Honnamachanahalli, Kunigal Taluk, Tumkur,
SCCH 15 6 MVC No.2168/2021 due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Lorry bearing Reg. No.KA520339?
2) Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay ?

3) What Order or Award?
7.
In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 44 documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P44.
Further, the Petitioner has examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.P45 & 46 and closed his side evidence.

On the other hand,
Respondent No.2 did not choose to lead evidence.

8. Having heard the arguments and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
SCCH 15 7 MVC No.2168/2021  Issue No.3 :

As per the Final Order,
 for the following :

REASONS 9. Issue No.1: It is the case of the Petitioner that, he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA520339 by its driver.

Gangadharaiah H.S vs Anand on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138655043/
3 10.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the offending Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA520339 by its driver.

11. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 44 documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P44 and he has reiterated the Petition averments in his Chiefaffidavit.
Ex.P1 to Ex.P6 are the True copies of FIR, Complaint, Spot mahazar, IMV Report, Wound Certificate, Charge sheet.
Ex.P7 to 9 are Discharge summaries and Ex.P10 is the Medical bills.

Ex.P11 to 44 are SCCH 15 8 MVC No.2168/2021 the OPD cards, Essential Certificate, Prescriptions, Xrays,
CT scan films, DL and OPD slip and Medical bills.

12. Upon going through the documents exhibited, Ex.P 1 & 2 are the True copies of the FIR & Complaint which shows that on the Complaint lodged by one Siddegowda S/o Late Javaregowda, the Huliyurdurga Police have registered the case against the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA520339 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279 and 337 of IPC.
Ex.P.3 is the true copy of Spot Mahazar which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P.4 is the IMV report which shows that the said accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles.
Ex.P.5 is the Wound certificate of the Petitioner which shows that the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries and the Petitioner initially treated in KIMS hospital, Bengaluru.

Ex.P.6 is the True copy of the Charge sheet which has been submitted by the Sub Inspector of Police, Huliyurdurga Police Station against the driver of the SCCH 15 9 MVC No.2168/2021 offending Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA520339 for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.
Ex.P.7 to 9, 37 & 38 are the Discharge summaries of the Petitioner.
Ex. P10
& 40 are the Medical bills.
Ex.P11 to 13 are the OPD cards.
Ex. P14
is the Essential Certificate.
Ex.P15 & 41 are the Prescriptions.
Ex.P16 to 29, 42 to 44 are the Xrays.
Ex.P30 to 35 are the CT scan films.
Ex . P36
is the copy of DL and Ex.P39 is the OPD slip.

13. The Petitioner has also examined the Doctor by name Dr. Ramesh B. as PW.2 and he has also reiterated the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a Road Traffic Accident and the treatment taken by the Petitioner.
14. PW.1 is subjected for cross examination by the Learned counsel for the Respondent No.2.

But,
nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of PW.1.
Further, the Respondent No.2 did not choose to lead any oral or documentary evidence to substantiate its Objection Statement SCCH 15 10 MVC No.2168/2021 contentions.
Hence, the Respondent No.2 has failed to substantiate its Objection Statement contentions.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioner has proved the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending lorry and in the said accident he had sustained injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.

Gangadharaiah H.S vs Anand on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138655043/
4 15.
Issue No.2:
As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
16. In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 30 years.
The Petitioner has produced his DL at Ex.P36, which shows his date of birth as 05.09.1989.
The accident has taken place on 17.01.2021.
Hence, at the time of accident, the Petitioner was aged about 32 years and the same to be taken for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
In the petition, the Petitioner has stated that he was working as a Driver and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/ per month.
But, he has not produced any document in this regard.
Therefore, in the absence of income proof, the notional income to be taken at Rs.15,000/ per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
18. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING :
19.

The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P5 issued by the Medical Officer of the Bhagawan Mahaveer Jain Hospital, Bengaluru shows that in the said accident the Petitioner has sustained following injuries i.e., SCCH 15 12 MVC No.2168/2021 1) Satured wound present over left lower limb extending from middle third of left leg anteriorly to distal third of left leg posteriorly for a length of 25cm, with swelling, tenderness and deformity of left leg.

2) Swelling and tenderness present over upper part of right arm.
3) Tenderness present over left chest region.
4) Tenderness present over the right chest region.

20. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of 1,00,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
II. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
21. Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of 50,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
SCCH 15 13 MVC No.2168/2021 III. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID-UP PERIOD:

Gangadharaiah H.S vs Anand on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138655043/
5 22.
The Petitioner deposed in his evidence that he had taken treatment at Bhagawan Mahaveer Jain Hospital, Bengaluru.

Upon going through Ex.P.7 to 9, 37 and 38  Discharge summaries of Bhagawan Mahaveer Jain Hospital, Bengaluru and Manipal Hospital shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient in the said hospital from 18.01.2021 to 28.02.2021, 08.03.2021 to 12.03.2021, 16.10.2021 to 17.10.2021, 20.09.2022 to 20.09.2022 and 08.11.2022 to 11.11.2022.
Therefore, while calculating the total period of which the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient, it comes to 52 days.
23. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as five months.

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled SCCH 15 14 MVC No.2168/2021 for compensation of 75,000/ under this head (@ 15,000/ per month ).
IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
24.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of 15,000/ (@ 100/ per day) towards attendants charges, 15,000/ towards extra diet and nourishment and 15,000/ towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.

In all,
the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 45,000/ under this head.

V.COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
25.
The petitioner has stated in his evidence that, he had spent huge amount towards medical and other incidental SCCH 15 15 MVC No.2168/2021 charges.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced medical bills and hospital bills at Ex.P10 & 40.
I have gone through the same and the same is acceptable.
Hence, by rounding off the same, the same to be taken at Rs.14,95,000/.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner is entitled for Rs.14,95,000/ under this head.
VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS / COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY:
26. The petitioner has stated that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and he is not able to do his work as he used to do earlier.
Even in his evidence, P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.

27. Further, the Petitioner got examined one witness by name Dr. Ramesh B. as P.W.2 who has deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a Road Traffic Accident and the treatment taken by him.

Further, he assessed the SCCH 15 16 MVC No.2168/2021 Permanent physical disability of the Petitioner towards left lower limb at 46% and 24% of right upper limb and whole body disability of the Petitioner at 28%.
PW.2 got marked OPD book and Xrays at Ex.P45 and 46.
In the crossexamination, he deposed that he has not treated the Petitioner and he has not seen the MLC record.

Further he deposed that he does not have information where the Petitioner Gangadharaiah H.S vs Anand on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138655043/
6 had taken treatment immediately after the accident.
Further he admitted that the injuries shown in the chief affidavit are the injuries found at the time of examination of the Petitioner in the Mahaveer Jain hospital on the next day of the accident.
Further he has deposed that he has not produced the Xray report.
He admitted that the fracture of the Petitioner is united.
He denied the other suggestions.

Having regard to the medical records placed on record, the evidence of P.W.2 and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 12% would be just and proper.
As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 16.

With multiplier of 16, income of 15,000/ per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 12%, the loss of future income comes to 3,45,600/ (15,000/ x 12 =
1,80,000/, 1,80,000/x 16 x 12/100 = 3,45,600/).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 3,45,600/ under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
29.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering  1,00,000/
2. Loss of amenities  50,000/
3. Loss of income during the laid  75,000/ up period 4.
Attendant's charges, Extra diet,  45,000/ and conveyance SCCH 15 18 MVC No.2168/2021 5.

Medical expenses 14,95,000/
6. Loss of Future Income  3,45,600/ Total 21,10,600/
30.
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of 21,10,600/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

31. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the Offending Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA520339.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.
The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1, has to pay the SCCH 15 19 MVC No.2168/2021 compensation amount to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".

Gangadharaiah H.S vs Anand on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138655043/
7 32.
Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of 21,10,600/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and SCCH 15 20 MVC No.2168/2021 interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E payment and after proper identification.
The remaining 25% award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of three years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/.
Draw Award accordingly.

(Dictated to the stenographer directly on the computer, print out taken by her,
corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the open Court on this the 13th day of August, 2024) (Smt. Kumari Sujatha.)
